rendered: Retention: the LLTO-2 coating kept the most capacity, 86.2%[1] of its initial discharge capacity after 200[2] cycles at 0.5C[3]. The pristine NCM retained only 56.6%[4] over the same cycles, so the LLTO-2 coating gave a much higher retention than the bare material. The other coatings were LLTO-0.5 at 85.5%[5] and LLTO-1 at 57.2%[6], which is barely above the pristine NCM. Rate capability: the paper says the LLTO coating first improved rate capability, but However, with 2 mol.% coating,[7] the rate capability decreased. The stated reason is that the coating layer became thicker, which suppressed electron transfer during charge and discharge: thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling[8]. The paper frames this with "may be due to", so it is a proposed explanation rather than a measured result. The same paper credits the general rate gain to the high ionic conductivity of the LLTO layer and to suppressed side reactions with the electrolyte.
